title: Plaque Assay For Screening Viral Concentrates for Bacteriophage
author: Dr. Steven Wilhelm
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.igxcbxn
materials: Pipet infected cells into molton top agar

steps.title: Prepare Bacterial Culture
steps.instruction: Grow a 4 mL liquid culture of the bacterial isolate of interest in an appropriate growth medium overnight.

steps.title: Prepare Culture for Assay
steps.instruction: Dilute the overnight culture 10-20% and allow it to grow for approximately 4 hours prior to the plaque assay.

steps.title: Prepare Top Agar
steps.instruction: Melt 0.6% top-agar in the microwave and let it cool for approximately 10-15 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Pipet 4 mL of molten top agar into sterile culture tubes
Keep top agar in a 45ºC head block to maintain a liquid state

steps.title: Process Bacterial Cells
steps.instruction: Prepare the bacterial cell suspension for the assay.

substeps.instruction: Pipet 1.5 mL liquid culture into 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes (or enough for 500 µL per plate sample)
Centrifuge for 2 min at 14,000 rpm (note: some isolates may not require centrifugation; determine empirically)
Resuspend the remaining cells in 1.5 mL BG-11 media and mix well with a pipet

steps.title: Inoculate Cells with Viral Concentrate
steps.instruction: Combine the resuspended cells with the viral concentrate and incubate.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL of 0.22 µm filtered viral concentrate to 500 µL of resuspended cells
Incubate for 15 min at the appropriate growth temperature for the bacterium in use
Vortex briefly, avoiding the formation of bubbles

steps.title: Plate and Incubate
steps.instruction: Cast the mixture into agar plates and incubate to observe plaques.

substeps.instruction: Pour top agar onto the plate and spread
Let agar solidify at room temperature for approximately 30-60 min
Flip plates over and place in an incubator at the appropriate growth temperature and light conditions for the bacterium in use

steps.title: Monitor for Plaques
steps.instruction: Check plates daily until a confluent lawn appears; plaques will be visible as obvious clearings.
